Natural Wood Tones Are Leading the Way

The biggest shift we’re seeing in 2025 is the move toward natural wood tone cabinetry. For years, white shaker cabinets dominated Orange County kitchens. They’re still popular, but more and more clients — especially in Newport Beach, Laguna Niguel, and Irvine — are asking for warm wood finishes that bring texture and character to the space.

White kitchens can feel cold and clinical. Natural wood adds warmth without sacrificing the clean, modern look that Orange County homeowners love. We’re seeing a lot of white oak and walnut-tone cabinets paired with lighter countertops to keep things balanced.

This Santa Ana kitchen remodel showcases custom natural wood shaker cabinets that add warmth and dimension while maintaining a clean, modern aesthetic.

Quartz Countertops Remain Popular in Orange County

Quartz remains the countertop material of choice for our Orange County clients, and for good reason. It’s durable, low-maintenance, and available in a huge range of colors and patterns. Unlike natural stone, quartz doesn’t need sealing, which matters when you’re spending $25,000 to $50,000 on a kitchen remodel.

We’re seeing a lot of interest in quartz options that mimic the look of Calacatta marble — the white base with dramatic grey veining. Clients get the elegant marble look without the maintenance headaches. For families with kids, quartz is practically a no-brainer.

This kitchen features quartz countertops with a Calacatta-style marble look, paired with classic white shaker cabinetry. The result is a bright, timeless space that offers the elegance of natural stone with the durability and low maintenance homeowners want for everyday living.
Open-Concept Kitchen Remodeling in Orange County Homes

The two most common layout changes we’re doing right now are opening up walls to create open-concept flow and adding or enlarging kitchen islands. Many homes in Orange County — especially in cities like Anaheim, Huntington Beach, and Santa Ana — were built in the 1970s-90s with closed-off kitchens separated from the living and dining areas.

Removing a non-load-bearing wall between the kitchen and living room is one of the highest-impact changes you can make. It immediately makes the space feel larger, brighter, and more connected. If the wall is load-bearing, we install a header beam — it adds cost but the result is worth it.

Islands are getting bigger too. Clients want seating for 3-4 people, built-in storage, and sometimes a secondary prep sink. If your kitchen footprint allows it, a large island becomes the centerpiece of daily life.

Matte Black Fixtures and Hardware

Matte black has become the dominant fixture finish across both kitchens and bathrooms. Faucets, cabinet pulls, light fixtures, shower heads — our clients are choosing matte black over brushed nickel and chrome. It creates a clean, modern contrast against lighter cabinets and countertops.

One thing we tell clients: commit to one finish throughout the room. Mixing matte black faucets with brushed nickel cabinet pulls looks disjointed. Pick one and carry it through every metal element in the space.

This bathroom remodel in Irvine features matte black faucets and mirror frames that create a striking contrast against the soft, neutral palette, giving the space a polished and contemporary feel.

Under-Cabinet LED Lighting

This is the most-requested “nice to have” feature we’re seeing. Under-cabinet LED strip lighting is affordable to install during a remodel and makes a noticeable difference in both function and aesthetics. It illuminates your countertop workspace and adds a warm ambient glow in the evenings.

We recommend LED strips with a dimmer switch and a warm white color temperature (2700K-3000K). Cool white LEDs under cabinets can make a kitchen feel like a hospital.

Bathroom Remodeling Trends: Frameless Glass and Freestanding Tubs

In bathrooms, two features are leading the 2025 requests: frameless glass shower enclosures and freestanding tubs.

Frameless Glass Shower Enclosures

Frameless glass showers open up the bathroom visually, making even smaller bathrooms feel spacious. They showcase your tile work instead of hiding it behind a curtain or frosted glass. The clean lines fit perfectly with the modern aesthetic Orange County homeowners are after.

Freestanding Tubs

Freestanding tubs are the statement piece in master bathroom remodels. They’re not just functional — they’re the focal point of the room. We’re installing them in master bath remodels across Laguna Hills, Mission Viejo, and Costa Mesa. Budget-wise, most of our bathroom remodels in Orange County land in the $20,000-$30,000 range.

This Laguna Hills master bathroom with frameless glass shower that highlights the tile work and a freestanding tub that serves as the focal point of the space.

Aging-in-Place Features Are Quietly Growing

While not every client asks for it, we’re seeing more homeowners — especially in communities like Laguna Woods and Mission Viejo — requesting aging-in-place features during their remodels. Curbless showers, comfort-height vanities, and wider doorways are easy to incorporate during a remodel and add long-term value to your home.

Our advice: even if you don’t need these features now, consider them during planning. It’s significantly cheaper to build them in during a remodel than to retrofit later.
